races.name: Blackmore Building Contractors Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Sea Of Charm
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner with pacemaking form at 13-15f trips, she handles Good and Standard going, has raced prominently in headgear (p), and returns after just 8 days — her ability to set an uncontested pace here is her primary asset and a straightforward lead is well within her grasp.

runners_data.name: Highland Harvey
runners_data.note: Smart trainer angle from Gihan Arnolda (0/2 T14 but recent winner at 12f on Good ground) and at just 4 years old this horse carries condition; he's a genuine hold-up type whose 1W4P sim-going record shows he can perform on Good but needs pace to chase, which may not materialise today.

runners_data.name: Stintino Sunset
runners_data.note: The Birkett yard is in decent nick (2/7 T14) and this 6-year-old has an excellent consistent record on Good ground (0W6P sim-going), racing prominently in headgear (h); 26 days since last run is mildly worth noting but the horse places reliably and deserves respect tracking the pace here.

runners_data.name: Wrist Art
runners_data.note: A 9-year-old hold-up type wearing tp headgear with modest form over this distance range on comparable going (0W3P sim-going); James Owen's yard has sent out a stream of runners (7/41 T14) without exceptional strike rate, and Wrist Art's best efforts have come over shorter than today's 1m4f trip.

runners_data.name: Little She
runners_data.note: Marcus Tregoning sends out a lightly-framed 4-year-old prominent racer in headgear (t) with two places from seven sim-going runs, mostly over 10f; stepping up to 1m4f is a question mark, but she has placed at 12f on Good before and the booking of a 5lb claimer keeps the weight competitive.

runners_data.name: The Pug
runners_data.note: Olly Murphy's runner has genuine form claims on his best Going-similar efforts (1W1P) but his natural hold-up style has been redistributed to a midfield slot because the field cannot accommodate all closers at the rear — this distorts his chance, and the [STYLE_FIT=0.92] flag indicates he is racing out of role, which on a track that doesn't flatter late finishers should temper confidence markedly.

races.paceDynamic: Sea Of Charm is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she will coast to the front from the off and control a comfortable, sustainable gallop over this 1m4f Brighton trip. Stintino Sunset and Little She will look to press from prominent positions, but neither has the pace or inclination to seriously disrupt Sea Of Charm's rhythm, meaning she dictates tempo on her own terms throughout. Highland Harvey, Wrist Art, and The Pug are all hold-up types, but the field holds more closers than the race shape can naturally accommodate at the rear — The Pug in particular has been redistributed to a midfield position it will not naturally find, and Highland Harvey will need a meaningful injection of pace to reel in the leader in time. This race shape heavily favours the front-runner and those racing prominently in a smoothly-run, uncontested lead scenario, where the absence of pressure rewards Sea Of Charm and makes life very difficult for true hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sea Of Charm Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Sea Of Charm breaks cleanly and is allowed to stride into an uncontested lead at a fair but controlled tempo.
scenarios.body: She settles on the front end with Stintino Sunset and Little She in her slipstream but never under serious pressure, leaving the hold-up horses with too much ground to close over the final two furlongs on this undulating track. This scenario is the dominant shape and firmly rewards the leader and the prominent horses who can track her home.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Outrun Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Stintino Sunset or Little She push forward aggressively early and force a contested pace, draining Sea Of Charm's reserves.
scenarios.body: A busier early gallop sees Sea Of Charm unable to maintain her lead turning into the final quarter-mile, and one of the prominent-tracking types swoops as she weakens late. This suits Stintino Sunset who has consistent form at this trip and handles Good ground well, and Little She who has been placed at longer distances before.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Get Into It Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the middle section and the field bunches, giving genuine hold-up horses a chance to close.
scenarios.body: Highland Harvey, with solid Good-ground form and a recent win at 12f, would be the most credible beneficiary as he has the class and tactical pace to pick off tiring rivals if the tempo sets up for closers. Wrist Art could be involved at big odds but his best runs have been over shorter trips and his form over this distance is modest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: The Pug Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If The Pug overcomes its redistributed midfield position and finds a clear run at the death in a truly-run race.
scenarios.body: Racing well out of its natural hold-up role and likely to find traffic from a midfield pitch, The Pug's chance depends on a confluence of pace collapses and clear passage that is unlikely given this field's construction. Its style-fit concern is real and the Brighton track's lack of a straight run-in punishes horses that need late momentum.

watchPoints.text: Sea Of Charm controls tempo entirely on her own — watch whether Mr Henry Main (3lb claimer) settles her early, as any rank behaviour or stumble on Brighton's undulating surface would immediately shift the race shape.

Highland Harvey needs a searching gallop to close from off the pace — if Sea Of Charm dictates a dawdle, watch for Liam McGaffin pushing him up much earlier than expected, potentially transforming him into a de facto prominent racer.

The Pug is being mapped to midfield against its natural style; watch at the start whether Josh Myers (7lb claimer, inexperienced) drops it out to its true hold-up position, stranding it with too much ground to make up on a track that punishes late runs.

Stintino Sunset has placed in six of its last fifteen sim-going starts without winning — watch whether Ross Birkett takes a more aggressive early position than usual to try to turn consistent placing into a first victory over this C&D configuration.

Wrist Art's headgear (tp, tongue-plus-cheekpieces) is a factor worth monitoring in the paddock — if the horse appears agitated or early racing ensues, the hold-up plan from Miss Criscuolo (5lb claimer) may be abandoned under pressure.

races.name: blackmorebuild.com EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Cruse On Bye
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with decent sim-going form (1/2 on Good) and trained by Attwater who has a 1/13 14-day strike rate — goes well fresh at 16 days since last run; needs Space Dreamer to come back to it but is ideally positioned to pounce from second.

runners_data.name: Tree Wizard
runners_data.note: Has placed twice on Good ground at five furlongs and handles this trip and going well (4/4 sim-going entries); jockey Abdulla Rashid Al-Hajri is an apprentice but Tree Wizard's consistency makes it the most reliable prominent threat, though 69 days off is a query.

runners_data.name: Water Angel
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha's yard is in solid form (5/25 T14) and Ray Dawson takes the ride; only one run (5th, 6f, Good) leaves form thin, but the hold-up style means it needs something to go wrong at the front end to get involved at Brighton.

runners_data.name: Last Dandelion
runners_data.note: Shown in midfield on the map but a genuine hold-up horse by nature — Stuart Williams's runner has a busy recent record (3 days since last run) and modest sim-going figures (3/7); racing forward of its comfort zone limits its chance in a shape set by the front-runner.

runners_data.name: Space Dreamer
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner, ridden by Billy Loughnane for Ollie Sangster (3/22 T14); both career runs produced 5th-place finishes but neither came in an uncontested lead scenario — getting a soft lead on a track that suits front-runners is a clear upgrade in conditions.

runners_data.name: Tricky Jenny
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with the best volume of form in the field but poor sim-going figures (1/5 on Good); Luke Morris rides for James Owen whose yard is in form (7/41 T14), yet Tricky Jenny has struggled on Good ground before and Brighton's layout does not flatter late closers.

races.paceDynamic: Space Dreamer is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no pressure expected from rivals, Billy Loughnane can control tempo from the outset on the downhill Brighton five-and-a-half furlongs, setting a sustainable gallop that keeps the race well within himself. Cruse On Bye and Tree Wizard will look to slot in behind from prominent positions, while Water Angel, Tricky Jenny, and Last Dandelion — the three hold-up types — will be tracking from further back. Brighton's undulating track rewards those who travel smoothly into the straight rather than those forced wide or late, meaning a controlled lead with a clean descent into the dip suits the front end of the field most. The field contains more hold-up horses than can truly operate from their natural rear positions, with Last Dandelion redistributed to midfield on the map — it is Last Dandelion who is most likely racing out of role, while the genuine hold-up types Water Angel and Tricky Jenny remain towards the rear. This race shape strongly favours prominent-to-leading runners who can maintain rhythm down the hill, with Space Dreamer and the prominent pair best placed to exploit an uncontested, measured pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Space Dreamer Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Space Dreamer bowls along uncontested and sets a fair but unhurried tempo down the hill.
scenarios.body: Loughnane slots into his rhythm unchallenged, covers the undulations efficiently, and has enough left to repel challengers entering the straight; prominent chasers Cruse On Bye and Tree Wizard are best positioned to benefit if he tires late but face a confident leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Reel Him In
scenarios.trigger: If Space Dreamer goes a fraction too fast early and Cruse On Bye or Tree Wizard travel better through the race.
scenarios.body: The leader hits the dip with something to find, and the prominent duo — having saved a length or two off the pace — pick up inside the final furlong on the favourable Brighton camber; Cruse On Bye's Attwater form and sim-going record gives it a slight edge here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or the prominent horses race too keenly and open a late gap for a finisher.
scenarios.body: Water Angel or Tricky Jenny, sitting furthest back, would need the front end to come back to them in the final furlong — Brighton's uphill finish can tighten, but the course more typically rewards position; Last Dandelion, racing out of its natural hold-up role in midfield, is poorly placed for a late swooping run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Shake-Up Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches on the descent, causing position losses and a scrappy contest with no clear tactical winner.
scenarios.body: Chaotic running order would theoretically open the race up for any runner at any price, but with only six runners and a clear pace setter this outcome is highly unlikely; Last Dandelion, already displaced from its natural position, represents the profile most at risk in a messy race.

watchPoints.text: Space Dreamer (Loughnane) — watch the early stride pattern leaving the stalls; if he bowls clear unchallenged within the first furlong, the race is likely set and the tactical picture is locked in.
Tree Wizard — 69 days off the track for a lightly-raced two-year-old; monitor paddock condition and early keenness, as an unfit or over-fresh run would remove one of the main prominent challengers.

Last Dandelion — ran just three days ago and is mapped to midfield despite being a natural hold-up horse; watch whether Marco Ghiani attempts to drop it back to its preferred position, which would leave it with even more to do on a track that punishes late runners.

Cruse On Bye — jockey James Glennon claims 7lbs; watch whether that weight advantage translates into a tactical ride that keeps the horse buried just behind the leader rather than forced wide on Brighton's camber.

Water Angel — sole runner for Dylan Cunha in this race; watch paddock behaviour for a second-time-out two-year-old who may have learned from its debut, as any significant market move would suggest stable confidence in improvement.

races.name: John Heal Memorial Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Dreams Galore
runners_data.note: Two wins on Good ground including over 6f make her the standout form pick; Billy Loughnane's claim keeps the weight attractive and Ollie Sangster's yard is 3/22 in the past 14 days — not red-hot but ticking over — and she simply has the clearest licence to control this from the front.

runners_data.name: Harry's Pop
runners_data.note: Ray Dawson partners a horse who just won over 6f on Good ground six days ago, suggesting Dylan Cunha's yard is in good nick; naturally prominent, he should slot into second gear directly behind Dreams Galore and is the most likely beneficiary if she tires.

runners_data.name: Cydney Sweenie
runners_data.note: Returned a placed effort over 6f on Standard and has Good-ground form to her name, but 46 days off the track is a concern for a juvenile and Jack Morland's yard is quiet in the short-term; a hold-up style makes her dependent on a stronger-than-expected gallop to deliver her challenge.

runners_data.name: Crowned
runners_data.note: Only three career starts means the form book is thin, but three consecutive placed efforts including a third on Good suggest a competent and improving type; Darragh Keenan will be aiming to get her into a rhythm from a midfield position and an each-way chance is not impossible if she steps forward again.

runners_data.name: Pageant Girl
runners_data.note: Her lone win came over 6f on Good ground and she holds the same trip and going combination here, but three consecutive single-figure finishes since that victory — including a tailed-off effort recently — make her reliability in question; Luke Morris will push her into a prominent role early given her style.

runners_data.name: Priscilla's Hope
runners_data.note: The hood is the key headgear flag here — she has worn it before and it may sharpen her focus — but OR 51 represents a significant class deficit even in this company, and five consecutive placed-or-worse efforts without a win make her a likely tail-ender despite the headgear switch.

races.paceDynamic: Dreams Galore is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no other horse likely to seriously contest her for the lead, she will stride out from the gates and control fractions over Brighton's 6f without being hassled. Harry's Pop and Pageant Girl will push into prominent positions just behind, creating a small three-horse cluster near the pace while Cydney Sweenie and Priscilla's Hope track them from the back half of the field. On Good ground at Brighton — a track that rewards horses travelling sweetly in touch — an uncontested pace of this nature tends to be measured rather than scorching, keeping the race competitive into the final two furlongs rather than stringing the field out early. This shape most directly favours prominent racers who can travel in the slipstream of Dreams Galore and pounce as she flattens out, rather than true hold-up horses who will face a stiff task generating enough momentum from off the pace on what is a relatively short sprint trip.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dreams Galore Front-Runs Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Dreams Galore dictates an uncontested, well-judged gallop and finds enough in the tank to hold on through the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Dreams Galore has won twice on Good ground over this course-and-distance profile, and with Billy Loughnane — who books well at this level — she can control the tempo precisely enough to deny the chasers a winning sprint angle; her OR of 71 gives her a clear class edge over this field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Dreams Galore's pace proves just fast enough to string the field out but ties herself up, allowing the prominent trackers to run over her inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Harry's Pop arrives with a recent win on Good ground over 6f and Ray Dawson can ensure he travels smoothly just off Dreams Galore's quarters; Pageant Girl, versatile over this trip on Good ground with a win to her name, gives trainer James Owen a live secondary chance in the same scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closer Gets Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to collapse the front-runners and create a sprint finish that suits horses coming from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Cydney Sweenie has shown placed form at 6f on Standard and has course-fitness questions after 46 days off, making this dependent on everything going perfectly in a race where the pace is unlikely to be truly searching; Priscilla's Hope wears a hood and plugs on without threatening but could grab minor honours if the pace truly collapses.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rank Outsider Upsets
scenarios.trigger: If the market leaders disappoint through inexperience or a rough trip and a lightly-raced type runs a career-best.
scenarios.body: Crowned is unexposed with only three runs and could improve sharply for Darragh Keenan if settled midfield and produced with a late run; the limited form sample makes this hard to quantify but the low OR of 63 conceals potential upside.

watchPoints.text: Dreams Galore's weight-for-age burden and the 14-day turnaround are manageable, but watch whether Billy Loughnane can resist going too fast too soon at Brighton — if she opens up fully by halfway she is vulnerable late.

Harry's Pop ran just six days ago; if he shows any sign of a bounce effect in the first furlong — slow to stride or lacking his usual prominent jump — the scenario that most suits him evaporates quickly.

Cydney Sweenie's 46-day absence is notable for a two-year-old; watch her pre-race demeanour and early movement — if she is bursting with freshness she may be more competitive than the form suggests, but if she looks ring-rusty she will struggle to land a blow from off the pace.

Pageant Girl's recent form has tailed off sharply, but James Owen's yard has a 7/41 strike rate over 14 days — reasonable volume — so check whether the trainer has flagged any stable confidence before dismissing her prominent draw entirely.

Priscilla's Hope's hood headgear change is worth monitoring in the paddock; any notable improvement in her demeanour or early stride pattern compared to recent lifeless efforts would be a reason to upgrade her very modest chance slightly.

races.name: Blackmore Equestrian Construction Handicap Stakes (Brighton Summer Sprint Series Final)

runners_data.name: Prefer The Sister
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up filly with six wins from good ground and an excellent recent record — six runs yielding three wins and two places — who will be ridden quietly off a fast pace; Christian Howarth's 3lb claim is useful and she has the closing kick to capitalise if the leaders empty.

runners_data.name: Dion Baker
runners_data.note: Front-running seven-year-old with five wins on good ground; Darragh Keenan will need to manage early scrimmaging with Kento and Candy Warhol — if he can find a rhythm rather than fight for the lead, his 0/5 trainer 14-day record is worth noting but his form figures 1,1 in his last two wins show he knows how to win.

runners_data.name: Twirler
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has placed twice in six 6f good-ground runs and won once at this trip on this going; Kieren Fox's booking is unexplained but his last run produced a placing over this exact course and distance combination which keeps him involved.

runners_data.name: Neptune Legend
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who has won on Firm and Good ground over 6f; David Egan's high-profile booking elevates interest and his last two wins came over 6f on Good, but he often needs things to fall perfectly and his 6f Brighton form record includes a recent sixth.

runners_data.name: Arnaz
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who has bolted up twice in succession over 6f on Good ground most recently; Billy Loughnane has a family yard angle and the horse is freshened up on just five days' rest — the back-to-back wins suggest he is in a purple patch, and his closing style suits if the pace truly bites.

runners_data.name: Secret Handsheikh
runners_data.note: Prominent-running eight-year-old wearing a visor; two recent wins over 5-6f on Good ground and a solid 9/15 good-going record make him very relevant, and Joe Leavy's booking for a small yard suggests confidence — he will look to grab a prominent berth early and hold it.

runners_data.name: Giant
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose last five runs have all been over longer trips of 7-8f; Harry Davies takes the ride but the step back to 6f is untested recently, and a winless good-ground record in this dataset makes him harder to support despite a couple of places.

runners_data.name: Kento
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with one win and five places on good ground; Marco Ghiani knows Brighton well and Kento's consistent placed record shows he stays competitive, but being one of three genuine leaders means he will have to burn energy early that may cost him late.

runners_data.name: Diomed Spirit
runners_data.note: Won over 6f Good and placed twice on similar ground recently; a natural closer whose true hold-up style means he is fighting against the race flow here — even with Saffie Osborne's ability to weave through traffic, gaining a clear run from deep in a 16-runner sprint is a significant ask.

runners_data.name: Big Time Rascal
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with three wins from ten good-ground starts over 6f and a 10/15 good-ground record; Luke Morris is a savvy big-field navigator and a horse who has placed or won in seven of his last ten 6f good-ground outings is a serious contender if he secures a front-rank position.

runners_data.name: Candy Warhol
runners_data.note: Front-runner who has not won on Good ground in his last five runs — his best form comes on Firm and Standard surfaces; he will push forward early but his Good-going record (0W1P from 3) raises a flag about whether he can sustain the effort to the finish.

runners_data.name: Washington Heir
runners_data.note: Young four-year-old whose most recent win came over this exact trip and going; a natural closer who will be forced forward by the crowded field — his 1W3P from 4 good-ground runs shows ability, but racing away from his comfort zone in a large, pace-pressured field reduces his chance markedly.

runners_data.name: Port Hedland
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up runner with one win over 6f Good in recent form; Myla Coppins takes a 5lb claim but the horse has been out of form (9,6,1,8 in last four) and in a race where closers are already compromised by being mapped forward, his lower OR of 48 makes him a difficult proposition.

runners_data.name: Bated Breeze
runners_data.note: Won over 6f Good last season and has recent placed form on Good ground; Gary and Josh Moore have an active yard with 2/16 in 14 days, but as a hold-up type forced into a midfield position, the horse needs traffic to part and a clear run that Brighton's undulations and a 16-runner field are unlikely to provide.

runners_data.name: Daley T
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with a blinker; his last five runs show no wins on Good ground and a modest 0W1P good-going record, and Tony Carroll runs four horses in this race which dilutes individual training focus — his high OR drop from previous runs and recent form string of 5,8,3,7,4,8 offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: My Boy Jack
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse in a visor whose last five runs span 6-7f on Good and Soft; Olivia Haines takes a 7lb claim which helps with the weight, but a 0W1P good-ground record and recent form of 4,5,0,3,4 over longer trips make him hard to support when genuine closers are already compromised by the race shape.

races.paceDynamic: Dion Baker, Kento, and Candy Warhol are all confirmed front-runners in a 16-runner sprint, making a strong early pace virtually guaranteed — Brighton's 6f undulating track will amplify the pressure as they battle for rail position from the off. Secret Handsheikh and Big Time Rascal will also look to press forward and claim prominent berths, meaning the front of the field will be intensely competitive through the first two furlongs. This relentless gallop will stretch the field early and test stamina in the closing stages, creating a race shape that classically favours horses who can sit just off the pace in a genuine prominent or close-midfield position, travelling smoothly without expending energy in the early battle. The field contains more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Diomed Spirit, Washington Heir, Port Hedland, Bated Breeze, Daley T, and My Boy Jack are all natural closers, but in this traffic-heavy, pace-saturated race, those needing a true hold-up trip are the least advantaged; the profile that benefits most is the off-pace prominent runner who can latch onto the speed without leading, conserve energy, and pounce as the leaders empty inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the three confirmed leaders burn each other out through a genuine scorching gallop and the field strings out early, allowing a well-positioned runner to reel in the spent pacemakers.
scenarios.body: Dion Baker, Kento, and Candy Warhol fight for supremacy and set a tempo that proves unsustainable on Brighton's testing undulations, leaving the race wide open to horses who have settled just behind and can produce a sustained finish. Runners who have prominent-but-not-lead profiles — and those with proven good-ground finishing kicks — are ideally placed to exploit the carnage at the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three leaders — most likely Dion Baker — manages to control the pace rather than being dragged into an all-out war and finds a rhythm that allows him to see out the six furlongs.
scenarios.body: With Dion Baker's rider Darragh Keenan able to slot in behind the other two early skirmishers and let them go, the seven-year-old with five wins on good ground could find his own pace before kicking clear from two out. This scenario rewards the horse with the best tactical gate-to-wire profile and genuine proven ability to win off a lead on this going.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Secret Handsheikh and Big Time Rascal manage to take up prominent berths just behind the battle of the three leaders and avoid the worst of the early scrimmaging.
scenarios.body: Both Secret Handsheikh and Big Time Rascal have strong recent records on good ground over six furlongs, and sitting second or third off a genuine pace gives them the perfect stalking position to strike as the leaders crack. This scenario particularly suits horses with visor or headgear assistance and high-strike-rate trainers who have them spot-on on the day.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Snatch Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so extreme that the race completely falls apart in the final furlong and a genuine hold-up finisher who has been shuffled back but travels wide and clear can pick off tired rivals.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape because the majority of the true hold-up horses — Diomed Spirit, Washington Heir, Port Hedland, Bated Breeze, Daley T, and My Boy Jack — are racing out of their natural role given the crowded midfield-to-rear, reducing the probability of a clean, late sweeping run. Even if the pace collapses entirely, the redistributed closers face a traffic puzzle that makes a clean passage from the rear extremely difficult to engineer.

watchPoints.text: Arnaz has won back-to-back on Good ground over 6f most recently and Billy Loughnane is in excellent form — watch whether he can settle off the hot pace and produce his now-trademark late surge, because if he does he could be the one to catch the leaders.

Secret Handsheikh is proven over 6f Good with two recent wins and wears the visor that has coincided with his best form — watch him grabbing a prominent position early, as he is the most dangerous stalker if Dion Baker and Kento burn each other out.

Dion Baker faces a direct early duel with Kento and Candy Warhol for the lead — watch the first furlong closely to see which of the three establishes dominance, because the one who does without a battle is the only true front-runner danger; if all three fight, none may last.

Big Time Rascal's Luke Morris is one of the most tactically astute jockeys in big-field handicaps — watch whether he is able to slot Big Time Rascal into second or third behind the lead battle, because that is the golden berth in this race shape and Morris has the experience to find it.

Tony Carroll saddles four runners (Neptune Legend, Kento, Washington Heir, Port Hedland, Daley T) in this race — watch for any signs of a stable runner being produced with a peak preparation, as Carroll's yard is 1/20 in 14 days but the sheer number of runners increases the chance of stable intelligence pointing to one specific horse.

races.name: Blackmore Design & Build Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Sea Suite
runners_data.note: Won over 7f Good at Brighton last time and again at 8f Good in the run before — this is her optimal track and trip combination; a front-running, or at worst prominent, style maps perfectly to this race shape and her visor (v) hints at a horse who needs to be kept focused, which Mason Paetel (5lb claim) should manage if she travels sweetly.|

runners_data.name: Knights Gold
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane takes the ride and brings strong recent credentials; a hold-up type by trade but with placed form at 8f Good he is versatile enough to track prominently in a small field, and his 2nd at 8f Good last time out suggests he retains his form well enough to be a live threat if he can sit just off Sea Suite.|

runners_data.name: Foreseen
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's horse has a win at 8f Good in recent form and Marco Ghiani is an accomplished big-track jockey; operating over a trip shorter than his best recent runs (10f this season) is a query, and as a genuine hold-up horse he needs a stronger pace than Sea Suite alone is likely to generate to get into the race late.|

runners_data.name: Dapper Guest
runners_data.note: David Egan picks up the ride on a horse whose recent form figures (8-6-4-0-8) are modest and whose last four at 7f show no win; a true closer by nature, he is placed in midfield on the map only because the rear of the field is overcrowded — his record of 0 wins from 15 similar-going starts is a serious flag regardless of pace shape.|

runners_data.name: North View
runners_data.note: Two placed efforts at 7f Good in recent history give this Tony Carroll-trained five-year-old a credible profile on paper; held up naturally but small-field dynamics mean Luke Morris may choose to press closer to Sea Suite than normal, and if he can get a position within a couple of lengths from the turn his closing run becomes more viable.|

runners_data.name: Cuban Lady
runners_data.note: Patrick Chamings's mare is stepping up from 5-6f to 7f and returning from 59 days off, both material concerns; Isobelle Chalmers carries a 7lb claim which softens the weight, and her three placed efforts at 6f Good are encouraging, but the extra furlong on a potentially fresh horse after nearly two months off creates too many unknowns to trust.|

runners_data.name: King Of War
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old with a win at 7f Good in his last five and solid course familiarity; his headgear (tp) and J F Egan's experience suggest he'll be produced late, but a 0-from-5 trainer record in the last 14 days and a field that is unlikely to collapse early mean his hold-up style faces a structural disadvantage here.|

races.paceDynamic: Sea Suite is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the early lead in this seven-strong field, she is expected to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop from the gates. Brighton's undulating 7f track — with its early descent and stiff finish — rewards a horse that can settle and dictate, and Sea Suite has won over this exact combination of course, distance and going. The redistributed hold-up quartet of Dapper Guest, North View, Cuban Lady and King Of War are all genuine closers by nature but are mapped to midfield because there is no meaningful front-running competition to chase Sea Suite and the rear of the field will be uncontested; of these, North View and Knights Gold are best-placed to track closer than their natural position suggests. A single uncontested leader setting a sensible pace over a distance that historically rewards front-runners at Brighton creates a race shape that strongly favours prominent racers who can track the leader within a length or two and kick from two furlongs out — deep closers relying on a strong pace to set up a late run will find conditions too straightforward and the tempo insufficient to bridge the gap.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sea Suite Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Sea Suite bowls along uncontested at a fair but not brutal gallop, dictating every yard to the home turn.
scenarios.body: Sea Suite controls the tempo, her rivals are forced to come to her rather than wait for a true end-to-end gallop, and her recent C&D form (1st at 7f Good and 1st at 8f Good) makes her very hard to pass when fresh and settled. Horses who track her closely — particularly Knights Gold from a prominent position — are best placed to pounce if she fades late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracked Closely, Late Kick
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent trackers — Knights Gold or North View — sits a length off Sea Suite and times their challenge perfectly inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The pace is honest enough to string the field out but not so strong that it collapses Sea Suite entirely; the horse who tracks closest has the momentum to overhaul her near the line. Knights Gold's recent placed form on Good and North View's 2nd and 3rd at 7f Good give both a plausible profile here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and Sea Suite ties up, allowing the hold-up runners to close from the rear in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: This is the least structurally likely shape given there is no genuine pace rival to force a collapse, but Foreseen's finishing kick and King Of War's course-distance win at 7f Good give them some hope if the fractions are unusually sharp. The redistributed hold-up horses would need to race far closer than their natural style to profit, which reduces the probability materially.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Pace, Midfield Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If Sea Suite is fractious or missed-beat at the start and the field bunches, creating a tactical, slowly-run affair.
scenarios.body: A slow or contested first three furlongs would compress the field and turn the race into a sprint home from the dip, bringing midfield types briefly into contention. Cuban Lady and Dapper Guest have the flat sprint profile to benefit from a muddled race, though their redistribution out of true hold-up positions and Cuban Lady's 59-day absence temper confidence significantly.

watchPoints.text: Sea Suite's early sectionals — if Mason Paetel allows her to stride clear unchallenged through the first two furlongs, the race is likely already won; watch whether any rival attempts to close the gap to within two lengths before the home turn.

Knights Gold's position at the start — Billy Loughnane may elect to sit closer than his horse's natural style dictates given the small field; if he slots in directly behind Sea Suite, his chance improves materially and changes the complexity of SCENARIO_A.

Cuban Lady's behaviour in the pre-parade and early stages after 59 days off — a fresh hold-up mare stepping up in trip is a risk factor; any sign of free-running or sluggishness will eliminate her from contention almost immediately.

The Tony Carroll stable has two runners (Foreseen and North View) — monitor any market moves or jockey instructions that suggest which is the yard's preferred runner, as they share the same form pool and the trainer may have clearer expectations about which suits this 7f Brighton test better.

races.name: Blackmore Proudly Sponsoring Brighton Racecourse Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Marsh Benham
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old hold-up specialist with solid Good-going form (2W3P in similar conditions from 15 runs), but Benoit de la Sayette rides just two days after a previous run — note the quick turnaround — and from the rear in a small field with a controlled pace, finding gaps may be the challenge.

runners_data.name: War Chant
runners_data.note: Callum Shepherd's mount carries headgear and has trainer Jack Jones in fine current form (2 from 15 over 14 days); a natural prominent racer who should secure second position behind Danehill Star, giving him the ideal tactical slot to pounce if the front-runner tires on this Good surface.

runners_data.name: Nordic Norm
runners_data.note: Returning from a 72-day absence for J.R. Jenkins (1 from 4 over 14 days), this four-year-old holds a headgear flag and has recorded only 0W0P from 13 similar-going runs — the layoff and limited course form make this a genuine unknown, and the slow-back record on comparable going is a concern.

runners_data.name: My Old Mate
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane's mount arrives in fine form (three wins in last six), but its natural instinct is to race from the rear — placed in midfield on the map because the field leaves no room at the back — meaning it will likely race closer than suits, and the STYLE_FIT score of 0.94 is a reminder to temper expectations in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Danehill Star
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's veteran (5 from 7 Good-going runs in the frame, 0 wins) is the sole front-runner and David Egan can dictate terms without challenge; the absence of any rival for the lead is the defining tactical fact of this race, and Danehill Star's consistent placed record on Good ground suggests it will not fold cheaply.

races.paceDynamic: Danehill Star is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-horse field and, with no genuine rival to challenge for the lead, David Egan should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop around Brighton's undulating mile. War Chant will look to sit prominently just off the pace, but with only one horse likely to set fractions, the tempo is unlikely to be truly searching. My Old Mate is a genuine hold-up type whose redistribution to midfield on the map reflects the reality that there are more hold-up horses in this field than the rear position can accommodate — Danehill Star is overwhelmingly likely to secure the lead, War Chant the prominent berth, leaving My Old Mate, Marsh Benham, and Nordic Norm to race further back than any of them might ideally want. A controlled pace set by a lone front-runner on Good ground over one mile at Brighton strongly favours horses with tactical versatility who can sit just off the pace and quicken, making the prominent-to-midfield profile the most dangerous.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Danehill Star Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Danehill Star dictates an unchallenged, controlled pace and the held-up horses cannot close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: Egan sets fractions to suit, building a rhythm that saps the closing kick from the hold-up horses in a small field with limited cover; War Chant, sitting closest, is best placed to capitalise if Danehill Star fades.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just brisk enough to stop Danehill Star but War Chant conserves energy in second and swoops at the furlong marker.
scenarios.body: War Chant's Good-ground figures, headgear, and proximity to the pace give him first run as Danehill Star tires; in a small, slowly run field, the horse in second position often gets first crack at the winner.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely moderate and a closer gets an unimpeded run to reel in the front-runner in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: My Old Mate arrives with strong recent form (three wins in last six), and if racing closer than usual — as the redistribution suggests — can produce a sharp late challenge on Good going over a trip that suits; however, racing out of natural role reduces confidence in this shape delivering.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If an unexpected tactical scramble unfolds and the small field compresses, leaving a chaotic sprint finish.
scenarios.body: With only five runners and one pace-setter, a truly bunched finish is unlikely but possible if Danehill Star goes too fast early and fades, causing a domino effect through the field; Nordic Norm, fresh off a 72-day break, is the unknown quantity who could benefit from a messy contest.

watchPoints.text: Danehill Star sets the pace unchallenged — watch whether David Egan elects to go fast enough to exploit the small field or conserves, because the fractions he sets will define every other horse's chance.
My Old Mate is racing out of its natural hold-up role due to redistribution — watch whether Billy Loughnane attempts to push forward or settles for a position that compromises its finishing kick.
Nordic Norm's 72-day absence combined with a record of 0W0P from 13 similar-going runs is a significant form concern — watch for any early signs of greenness or lack of match fitness.

War Chant's headgear and Good-going record (1W3P from 5 runs) make it the horse most likely to be in the ideal tactical position throughout — watch whether it can maintain proximity to Danehill Star without expending energy.

With only five runners, the race is vulnerable to a very slow early pace that compresses the field — watch the opening two furlongs to determine whether this becomes a tactical crawl or a genuine test of stamina.
